name: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd

profile.description: Credo Technology designs high-speed connectivity for AI and cloud data centers: active electrical cables (AECs), optical PAM4 DSPs, line-card PHYs, SerDes chiplets and SerDes IP licensing, built on proprietary SerDes and DSP technology. FY2026 (ended May 2, 2026) revenue tripled to $1.34B from $437M with GAAP net income of $472M. Q1 FY2027 revenue was $479M (+115% YoY) and Q2 guidance is $525-535M, with optical revenue targeted above $600M for FY2027. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in San Jose with a Cayman Islands domicile, Credo has a market cap of about $28B after the stock fell to $150.99, well below its 52-week high of $308.67.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Credo moved from SerDes IP licensing into system-level products and created the AEC category, taking revenue from $58.7M in FY2021 to $1.34B in FY2026 and from a $28M net loss to $472M of GAAP net income [3]. AI Deployment (2/2): Its AECs, optical DSPs and retimers ship into hyperscaler AI clusters, and Q1 FY2027 revenue of $479M grew 114.7% YoY on that demand [1]. Market Share (2/2): As the originator and leading supplier of AECs for AI rack connectivity, Credo is the fastest share gainer in the category, with revenue growing far faster than larger connectivity peers [1][3]. Pipeline (1/2): Management is targeting more than $600M of optical revenue in FY2027 and is ramping 200G-per-lane 1.6T solutions, but those depend on scarce 3nm silicon and research found no dated launch schedule [1][5]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2026 R&D was $279M, or 20.9% of revenue, in line with high-performance semiconductor peers even as revenue tripled [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Credo states a clear mission of delivering high-speed, energy-efficient connectivity solutions, which describes what it does and for whom but does not articulate a deeper purpose [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No quantified foundation or community-investment program was found. Employee Retention (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong: Chairman, President and CEO Bill Brennan has led Credo from startup to public company over more than a decade, and co-founder CTO Chi Fung Cheng remains in place, but no company-wide retention data was found [5][7]. Insider Buying (0/2): Insiders are consistent sellers, with 123 disposals and zero purchases over 90 days as of June 2026, including Brennan's sale of 54,984 shares for about $12M on June 5 and COO Yat Tung Lam's 50,000-share sale on July 15, mostly under 10b5-1 plans [6].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on all 7 growth metrics; every metric meets or beats its target. D/E is 0.96% (1.0), ROE is 30.7% (1.0, 2x weight), revenue growth is 114.7% YoY (1.0), and the FY2021-FY2026 revenue CAGR is 86.8% (1.0, 2x weight; derived from FMP annual statements, $58.7M to $1.34B) [2][3]. After the selloff, forward P/E is 15.5 (1.0), TTM net margin is 33.8% (1.0), and FMP's forward PEG of 0.57 (1.0, 2x weight) shows the price is low relative to expected earnings growth [2][8]. Weighted sum 10.0/10 = 10. Liquidity floor easily cleared: 7.63M avg daily volume at $150.99 is about $1.15B per day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Credo is AI infrastructure. Its cables, DSPs and retimers are the physical links that let GPUs, switches and memory talk to one another inside AI clusters, so more AI compute means more demand for its products, which is why Q1 FY2027 revenue more than doubled [1]. The risks analysts flag are AI-capex cyclicality and customer concentration, not AI substitution [6]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Nearly all of the $479M Q1 FY2027 revenue comes from AI and hyperscale data-center connectivity, and management targets more than $600M of optical revenue in FY2027 [1].

infinite_game.summary: Credo shows the existential flexibility Sinek admires: it bet the company on turning from IP licensing into a system-level hardware supplier, and the founding team still runs it. But its purpose reads more like a product description than a Just Cause, insiders sell steadily, and the CEO's new award is tied to revenue and share-price targets. Its endurance has not yet been tested by an AI-capex downturn.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Credo's push for high-speed, energy-efficient connectivity is a genuine cause that has guided product choices, from inventing AECs to its move into optical DSPs [1][4]. Leadership references it consistently, but it is closer to a technical mission than a vision of a better world, and it has not yet been tested through a major industry downturn.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The CEO and founding CTO have stayed in place through the startup, IPO and hypergrowth phases, and headcount has grown to 807 [5][7]. No employee-sentiment or turnover data was found, so the organization is rated stable but not demonstrably high-trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Research found no management commentary that frames competitors such as Broadcom or Marvell as benchmarks to learn from. Coverage centers on valuation comparisons with peers and on supply constraints, not on how rivals shape Credo's own improvement [5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Credo reinvented itself from a SerDes IP licensor into a maker of AECs, chiplets and optical DSPs, a change that redefined its business model and grew revenue more than 20-fold between FY2021 and FY2026 [3]. Its current expansion from copper into optical, targeting more than $600M of optical revenue in FY2027, is a second strategic evolution [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Credo kept investing heavily in R&D through years of losses ($95.5M of R&D in FY2024 against a $28M net loss) to build the AEC market ahead of demand [3]. More recently, the June 2026 CEO award tied to a $2.5B revenue goal and a $244.70 share price, alongside steady insider selling, points to targets measured in revenue and stock price rather than costly long-term sacrifice [5][6].

investment_thesis: Credo is a direct play on AI data-center connectivity. FY2026 revenue tripled to $1.34B with GAAP net income of $472M, Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 114.7% to $479M with non-GAAP EPS of $1.20 versus $0.52, and Q2 guidance of $525-535M implies continued sequential growth [1][3]. Optical revenue is targeted above $600M for FY2027, adding a second growth engine beyond copper AECs [1]. After a roughly 50% decline from the $308.67 high, the stock trades at 15.5x forward earnings with an FMP forward PEG of 0.57, on a balance sheet with almost no debt (D/E 0.96%) and a 33.8% net margin [2][8].
thesis_continued: The bear case is concentration and cyclicality. About 90% of revenue reportedly comes from the top 10 customers, so one hyperscaler pause or design loss would hit hard, and the stock's 5-year beta of about 3.2 amplifies any slowdown in AI capex [5][6][8]. GAAP gross margin fell sequentially in Q1 FY2027 and guidance of 62.9-64.9% shows continued pressure, inventory has grown to about $208M, and 200G-per-lane products depend on constrained 3nm capacity [1][5][6]. Insiders keep selling (123 disposals, no purchases over 90 days), and larger rivals such as Broadcom and Marvell have far more R&D resources [6].
key_catalysts: Q2 FY2027 results against $525-535M revenue guidance and gross margin of 62.9-64.9% GAAP / 67-69% non-GAAP [1]
Optical portfolio ramp toward the more-than-$600M FY2027 target, broadening Credo beyond copper AECs [1]
Ramp of 200G-per-lane 1.6T solutions as hyperscalers move to next-generation AI fabrics, with management comfortable on capacity through 2027 [5]
key_risks: Customer concentration, with about 90% of revenue reportedly from the top 10 customers and two above 10% each, exposing Credo to any hyperscaler capex pause or design-out [6]
Gross-margin compression (GAAP gross margin guided to 62.9-64.9%) and inventory of about $208M, up from $26M two years earlier [1][6]
High volatility (beta about 3.2) and persistent insider selling, after a fall of about 50% from the $308.67 52-week high [6][8]
